A food additive code listed without a specific common name, used in food for its listed technical function.
Guar gum is a polysaccharide extracted from the seeds of the guar plant. It is used to thicken foods and to keep ingredients from separating.
A gum obtained from the dried sap of Astragalus shrubs, used to thicken, stabilize, and emulsify foods such as sauces and dressings.
Acacia gum is a natural gum harvested from the sap of acacia trees, used to carry flavors, emulsify mixtures, and thicken foods.
Xanthan gum is a polysaccharide produced by fermenting sugar with a bacterium. It is used to thicken liquids and keep mixtures from separating.
A plant gum obtained from the sap of Sterculia trees, used to thicken, stabilize and emulsify sauces and dressings.
A plant gum obtained from the seeds of the tara shrub, used as a stabilizer and thickener in foods.
Gellan gum is a thickening and stabilizing agent produced by bacterial fermentation, used to give foods a gel-like or smooth texture.
A sugar alcohol made from glucose, used to add sweetness, retain moisture, and give foods body and texture.
D-sorbitol is a sugar alcohol made from glucose that is used as a sweetener, humectant and thickener, helping foods retain moisture and texture.
A liquid form of sorbitol, a sugar alcohol made from glucose, used as a sweetener, humectant and thickener to retain moisture and add body to foods.
A sugar alcohol that occurs naturally in some plants and is made commercially, used as a humectant, sweetener, and thickener in foods.
Glycerol is a simple sugar alcohol that can be made from plant or animal fats, and it is used in food to retain moisture and add thickness.
A thickening plant fiber obtained from the root of the konjac plant, used to hold water, stabilize and thicken foods.
A thickening fiber derived from the root of the konjac plant that absorbs water and helps stabilize foods and form gels.
A soluble fiber extracted from the root of the konjac plant, used as a thickener, stabilizer, emulsifier, and humectant in foods.
A plant gum obtained from the seeds of the cassia tree, used as an emulsifier, stabilizer, and thickener. It is vegan and vegetarian.
A protein obtained by partially breaking down collagen from animal skin, bones and connective tissue, used to gel, thicken and stabilize foods. The taxonomy marks it as an animal-derived ingredient.
Peptone is a mixture of protein fragments produced by breaking down proteins, used as a nutrient source and to add body and flavor. It is considered suitable for vegans and vegetarians.
Polyoxyethylene (40) stearate is a synthetic emulsifier made by combining ethylene oxide with stearic acid, used to keep oil and water mixed in foods. Its vegan and vegetarian status is unclear.

Polyoxyethylene sorbitan monolaurate is a synthetic emulsifier made by attaching ethylene oxide to sorbitan esterified with lauric acid, used to keep oil and water blended. Its fatty acid source may be animal or plant based.

A synthetic nonionic surfactant made from polyethoxylated sorbitol and oleic acid, used to blend oil and water and stabilize food mixtures. Its vegan and vegetarian status is uncertain from the available data.
Polyoxyethylene sorbitan monopalmitate is a synthetic emulsifier made from sorbitol and palmitic acid, used to keep oil and water mixed in foods.
A synthetic emulsifier made from sorbitan stearate reacted with ethylene oxide, used to keep oil and water mixed and to stabilize foams.
A synthetic emulsifier made by attaching ethylene oxide chains to sorbitan and esterifying it with stearic acid. It helps oil and water mix and keeps mixtures stable.
Pectins are naturally occurring plant fibers, typically extracted from fruit peel, that form gels and thicken foods such as jams and jellies.
A plant-derived additive used as an emulsifier, stabilizer, and thickener in foods. It is vegan and vegetarian.
A pectin that has not been chemically treated with ammonia, a plant-derived polysaccharide used as an emulsifier, stabilizer, and thickener in foods.
Amidated pectin is a modified form of pectin, a plant-derived polysaccharide, used to thicken and stabilize jams, jellies, and dairy products.
A glycerol-based emulsifier made by treating hydrogenated rapeseed oil with glycerol, used to keep oil and water mixed in foods such as spreads and baked goods.
Ammonium phosphatides are a mixture of phospholipids made from vegetable oils, used as an emulsifier to help oil and water mix in food.
A synthetic chemical made by adding bromine to vegetable oil, formerly used to keep flavoring oils evenly mixed in citrus-flavored drinks.
A synthetic ester of sucrose used to help oil and water mix and to keep food textures consistent.
An emulsifier and stabilizer made by esterifying glycerol with rosin acids obtained from pine wood resin, used in beverages and other foods.
A group of phosphate salts used to stabilize texture, retain moisture and help emulsify ingredients in processed foods.
Disodium diphosphate is a sodium salt of pyrophosphoric acid that stabilizes texture, binds water, and helps hold ingredients together in foods.
Trisodium diphosphate is a sodium phosphate salt used to stabilize texture, retain moisture, bind ingredients together, and control acidity. Its vegan and vegetarian status is not specified.
A sodium salt of pyrophosphoric acid. It is used to help emulsify, thicken, stabilize, and retain moisture in foods and to bind metal ions.
A potassium salt of diphosphoric acid used to help emulsify, thicken, and stabilize food texture and to bind moisture.
A calcium phosphate compound used as an emulsifier and stabilizer to help ingredients mix and keep food texture consistent.
Calcium dihydrogen diphosphate is a calcium salt of diphosphoric acid used to stabilize and thicken foods and to bind metal ions, while helping to keep moisture in place.
A group of phosphate salts used in foods to retain moisture, keep ingredients blended, and stabilize texture.
A sodium phosphate salt that helps bind water, keep ingredients mixed together, and preserve a smooth texture in processed foods.
Pentapotassium triphosphate is a potassium salt of triphosphoric acid used as an emulsifier, thickener and stabilizer that helps bind water and metal ions.
A group of salts of phosphoric acid, used to emulsify, retain moisture, bind metal ions, and thicken or stabilize foods.
Sodium polyphosphate is a family of inorganic sodium phosphate salts used to bind water, stabilize emulsions, and thicken foods.
Potassium polyphosphate is a salt of phosphoric acid used as an emulsifier, thickener and stabilizer that helps keep ingredients mixed and binds metal ions.
A calcium salt of polyphosphoric acid used to bind minerals, retain moisture and thicken or stabilize foods.
Sodium tripolyphosphate is an inorganic sodium phosphate salt used to retain moisture, bind metal ions, and stabilize texture in foods.
Alpha-cyclodextrin is a ring-shaped sugar molecule made from starch by enzyme treatment. It is used as a stabilizer and thickener in food.
A plant-derived polymer of glucose that forms the structural fiber of plant cell walls, used as a thickener, stabilizer and carrier in foods.
A purified form of plant cellulose broken into fine particles. It is used as a bulking agent, thickener, and stabilizer, and to carry other ingredients.
Cellulose from plant fiber that has been ground into a fine powder, used as a bulking agent, thickener, and anti-caking agent.
A cellulose derivative made by chemically modifying plant cellulose, used as an emulsifier, stabilizer and thickener that helps hold ingredients together and adds body to foods.
A synthetic cellulose derivative used as a carrier for flavors and colors and to thicken foods.
Hydroxypropyl cellulose is a modified cellulose derived from plant fiber, used as an emulsifier, stabilizer and thickener in foods.
A modified plant-derived cellulose that forms a gel or thickens when mixed with liquids, used to improve texture and stability.
Sodium carboxy methyl cellulose is a modified plant cellulose in the form of a sodium salt, used to thicken, stabilize, and retain moisture in foods.
Cross-linked sodium carboxymethylcellulose is a chemically modified cellulose derivative used to stabilize and thicken foods.
A modified form of cellulose, the plant fiber from which carboxymethylcellulose is derived, treated with enzymes to shorten its chains, used to stabilize and thicken foods.
Sodium, potassium, calcium, and magnesium salts of fatty acids are emulsifiers made from fats and oils that help blend ingredients and keep foods smooth.
Sodium, potassium and calcium salts of fatty acids are soap-like compounds made from fats and oils, used to emulsify, stabilize and thicken foods.
Sodium salts of fatty acids are compounds formed from fatty acids and sodium. They help mix oil and water and keep food textures uniform.
Calcium salts of fatty acids are compounds formed from fatty acids and calcium. They act as emulsifiers, stabilizers and thickeners in foods.
Magnesium salts of fatty acids, used as emulsifiers, stabilizers and thickeners to keep food ingredients from separating.
E470iii is a fatty acid salt additive, a group of compounds made from fatty acids and metal ions. It is used to emulsify, stabilize and thicken foods.
Mono- and diglycerides of fatty acids are fat-derived emulsifiers made by partially reacting glycerol with edible fatty acids. They help oil and water stay mixed and give foods a smoother texture.
Acid esters of mono- and diglycerides of fatty acids are emulsifiers made by reacting glycerol-based fats with acids, used to blend oil and water and improve texture in foods.

A mixture of fatty acid esters made from glycerol and acetic acid, used as an emulsifier and stabilizer in baked goods, whipped toppings and similar foods. Its source may be animal or plant fat, and it is not confirmed to be vegan or vegetarian.
A mixture of lactic acid esters with mono- and diglycerides of fatty acids, used to blend oil and water, keep texture even, and bind metal ions in food.
Citric acid esters of mono- and diglycerides are emulsifiers made from glycerides of fatty acids reacted with citric acid, used to blend fats with water and stabilize texture in baked goods.

Tartaric acid esters of mono- and diglycerides of fatty acids are emulsifiers made by reacting fatty acid glycerides with tartaric acid, used to blend fats and water and improve dough texture. Their vegan and vegetarian status depends on the fat source used.
A mixture of esters made from fatty acids, glycerol and tartaric acid, used as an emulsifier and stabilizer to keep oil and water ingredients mixed in baked goods.

Succinylated monoglycerides are emulsifiers made by reacting monoglycerides of fatty acids with succinic acid, used to improve texture, blend ingredients and extend shelf life. Their vegan and vegetarian status depends on the fat source used.
A family of esters made from sucrose and fatty acids, used as an emulsifier and stabilizer that helps oil and water mix in foods. Its source may be animal or plant based.
Sucroglycerides are fat-derived emulsifiers made by combining sugar with glycerides, and they help oil and water stay mixed in foods.
A group of fat-based compounds made by combining glycerol with fatty acids, used to blend oil and water and keep mixtures stable. Source may be plant or animal fats.
A synthetic emulsifier made by chemically modifying castor oil fatty acids, used to keep oil and water mixed in foods such as chocolate and spreads.
Propane-1,2-diol esters of fatty acids are emulsifiers made by reacting propylene glycol with fatty acids, used to blend oil and water and to give foods a smoother texture.
This additive is a reaction product of heat-oxidised soybean oil with mono- and diglycerides of fatty acids. It is used as an emulsifier to help oil and water mix in foods.
A manufactured emulsifier made by combining stearic acid with lactic acid, used to help oil and water blend and to improve dough texture.
Calcium stearoyl-2-lactylate is a calcium salt made by combining stearic acid with lactic acid, used in food as an emulsifier and stabilizer. Its source fats may be animal or plant based.
Calcium stearoyl lactylate is a compound made by combining stearic acid and lactic acid with calcium, used as an emulsifier to help mix fats and water-based ingredients in baked goods.
Stearyl citrate is an ester formed from citric acid and stearyl alcohol, a fatty alcohol. It is used as an antioxidant, emulsifier and sequestrant to slow spoilage and bind metal ions.
Calcium stearoyl fumarate is a calcium salt of a fumaric acid and stearic acid compound. It is used as an emulsifier and dough conditioner in baked goods.
Sodium dodecyl sulfate is a synthetic surfactant, a compound that helps mix oil and water, used as a foaming and emulsifying agent.
E490 is a food additive from the E-number system whose exact chemical identity is not described in this listing, and it is considered suitable for vegans and vegetarians.
Sorbitan monostearate is an ester of sorbitol and stearic acid, used as an emulsifier to keep oil and water mixed in foods; its animal or plant origin varies by manufacturer.
An ester of sorbitol and stearic acid, used to blend oil and water and keep mixtures stable. Its source may be animal or plant based.
An ester formed from sorbitol, a sugar alcohol, and lauric acid, used as an emulsifier and stabilizer to help ingredients that do not normally mix stay blended.
An ester formed from sorbitol, a sugar alcohol, and oleic acid, used as an emulsifier and stabilizer to keep oil and water components evenly dispersed in food.
Sodium carbonates are sodium salts of carbonic acid, typically produced as a white powder. They are used to adjust alkalinity and to stabilize and thicken certain foods.
An inorganic salt also known as soda ash, used to adjust alkalinity and to help foods hold their structure and texture.
Sodium hydrogen carbonate is a white crystalline salt, commonly known as baking soda. It is used to stabilize and thicken foods and to adjust acidity.
Sodium sesquicarbonate is a mineral compound of sodium carbonate and bicarbonate, used to stabilize and thicken foods.
A potassium salt of carbonic acid, a white alkaline powder. It is used as a stabilizer and to adjust alkalinity in foods.
A potassium salt of carbonic acid, used as a stabilizer and to adjust alkalinity in foods such as cocoa and noodles.
A mineral salt, also called potassium bicarbonate, used to regulate acidity and help baked goods rise.
Carbonates are salts of carbonic acid, such as sodium or calcium carbonate, used to regulate acidity, act as leavening agents, or serve as anticaking agents.
A compound of ammonia and carbon dioxide used as a leavening agent that releases gas when heated, helping baked goods rise.
A white crystalline compound of ammonia and carbon dioxide used as a leavening agent that releases gas when heated, helping baked goods rise.
A leavening agent, a white salt that releases carbon dioxide gas when heated, helping baked goods rise.
Magnesium carbonates are white mineral salts of magnesium and carbonate that are added to other ingredients to help them flow freely and stay dispersed.
Magnesium carbonate is a white mineral compound of magnesium and carbonate, used in foods as a carrier that helps spread other additives evenly.
Magnesium hydroxide carbonate is an inorganic magnesium compound. It is used as a carrier that helps distribute other food ingredients evenly.
Hydrochloric acid is a strong, colorless aqueous solution of hydrogen chloride that is used to adjust acidity during food processing.
Potassium chloride is a mineral salt that is used as a salt substitute, stabilizer, thickener, and preservative in processed foods.
A mineral salt of calcium and chloride that helps foods set, firm up, and keep their texture, often used in cheese and canned produce.
Ammonium chloride is a white crystalline salt used in food as a flavoring agent and as a dough conditioner that adjusts the acidity and texture of baked goods.
Magnesium chloride is a mineral salt that stabilizes food texture and causes proteins to coagulate, often used in tofu production.
Stannous chloride is a tin compound used as an antioxidant to slow spoilage and color changes in foods. It is considered suitable for vegans and vegetarians.
Sulphuric acid is a strong mineral acid used in food processing as an acidity regulator and in the preparation of certain ingredients.
Sodium sulphates are sodium salts of sulfuric acid used in food processing as a mineral additive that can adjust texture and mineral content.
A white crystalline salt of sulfuric acid and sodium, used as a filler and to adjust the bulk of food ingredients.
Sodium hydrogen sulphate is an acidic sodium salt of sulphuric acid, used in food to adjust acidity and act as a processing aid.
Potassium sulphates are mineral salts of potassium and sulphur used as a source of potassium and to adjust the mineral content of certain foods.
Potassium sulphate is a mineral salt of potassium and sulfuric acid. It is used in food processing as a salt substitute and firming agent.
A mineral compound of calcium and sulphate that binds metal ions and stabilizes texture in foods, often used to firm up tofu and canned vegetables.
A white crystalline salt formed from ammonia and sulphuric acid, used in food mainly as a processing aid and to adjust acidity in ingredients such as flour.
An inorganic compound of aluminium and sulfate, used in food processing as a firming and acidity-regulating agent.
A mineral salt of aluminium and sulphate. It is used as a firming agent and acidity regulator in some foods.
Aluminium potassium sulphate is a mineral compound of aluminium, potassium and sulphate, used in food as a firming agent and to help control acidity.
Aluminium ammonium sulphate is a double salt of aluminium, ammonium and sulphate that is used as a stabilizer in some processed foods.
A strong alkaline compound used to adjust acidity, peel produce, and process cocoa and other foods.
Potassium hydroxide is a strong alkaline compound of potassium used to adjust pH and to process cocoa and other foods.
Calcium hydroxide is an alkaline mineral compound, also called slaked lime, used to adjust acidity, firm textures, and process foods such as corn for masa.
Ammonium hydroxide is an aqueous solution of ammonia. It is used as an alkali to adjust acidity in food processing.
A white mineral compound made from magnesium and water, used as an alkali to adjust acidity and as an anti-caking agent in foods.
Calcium oxide, also called quicklime, is a white mineral compound used to adjust acidity and to firm or process foods.
Magnesium oxide is a white mineral compound used in food as an anticaking agent, acidity regulator, and source of magnesium.
A yellow crystalline compound of iron, cyanide and sodium, used as an anti-caking agent to keep salt and similar powders from clumping.
A yellow crystalline compound of iron, cyanide and potassium, used as an anti-caking agent to keep salt and similar powders free-flowing.
Sodium thiosulfate is a sodium salt of thiosulfuric acid used to slow oxidation and bind metal ions that could otherwise spoil food.
A leavening acid salt of aluminium and phosphate that reacts with baking soda to release gas and also stabilizes and thickens foods.
A mineral salt containing aluminium, sodium and phosphate, used as an acidifying agent in leavening systems and as an emulsifier, stabilizer and thickener.
A calcium phosphate compound obtained from animal bone, used as an emulsifier and humectant that helps foods retain moisture and keep ingredients blended.
Sodium silicate is a compound of sodium oxide and silicon dioxide, supplied as a glassy solid or liquid, that is used as an anti-caking and processing agent.
Sodium metasilicate is an inorganic sodium silicate compound. It is used in food processing as an alkali and cleaning-related agent to adjust pH.
Silicon dioxide is a fine, inert mineral powder, used as an anti-caking agent and carrier to keep powdered foods free-flowing.
A white mineral compound made of calcium and silicon oxygen. It is used as an anti-caking agent to keep powdered foods free-flowing.
A group of magnesium salts of silicic acid that is added as a thickener and anti-caking agent to dry and powdered foods.
Talc is a naturally occurring mineral made of magnesium silicate, used in food as a thickener and anti-caking agent.
A synthetic mineral compound of sodium, aluminum and silicon, used as an anti-caking agent to keep powdered foods free-flowing.
Potassium aluminium silicate is a mineral compound of potassium, aluminum and silicon, used in foods as an anti-caking agent to keep powders free-flowing.
Bentonite is a clay mineral composed mainly of aluminum silicate, used in foods to clarify liquids such as wine and juice by helping particles settle out.
Aluminium silicate is a mineral compound of aluminium and silica that is used as an anti-caking agent to keep powdered foods free-flowing.
A compound of potassium and silica that is used as an anti-caking agent, keeping powdered foods from clumping.
Fatty acids are carboxylic acids derived from fats and oils, used in foods as emulsifiers, release agents, or processing aids; their source may be animal or plant based.
A salt of magnesium and stearic acid that is used as an anti-caking and lubricating agent, helping powders flow freely and preventing them from sticking to equipment.
Aluminium stearate is a metal soap made from aluminium and stearic acid, used as a thickener, stabilizer and anti-caking agent in food.
A mild organic acid produced by fermenting glucose, used to add a slightly tart taste and to help control acidity in food.
A substance formed from glucose that releases a mild acid when dissolved, used to control acidity and bind metal ions in foods.
The sodium salt of gluconic acid, a substance made by fermentation of glucose. It binds metal ions and helps foods keep their texture and consistency.
Potassium gluconate is the potassium salt of gluconic acid, which is produced by fermentation of glucose. In food it is used as a sequestrant that binds metal ions.
A calcium salt of gluconic acid, used as a sequestrant that binds metal ions and helps keep foods stable.
An iron salt of gluconic acid, used as a nutrient to add iron to foods and as a color-retention agent in some olives.
A salt of gluconic acid and magnesium, used as a source of magnesium and as a firming agent in some foods and supplements.
An iron salt of lactic acid used as a nutrient supplement to add iron to foods and correct iron deficiency.
Glutamic acid is an amino acid that occurs naturally in many proteins, and in food it is used mainly to add savory flavor.
The sodium salt of glutamic acid, a substance that occurs naturally in many foods and is added to enhance savory, umami flavor.
Monopotassium glutamate is the potassium salt of glutamic acid, an amino acid, and is used to add savoury flavour to foods.
A salt of glutamic acid and ammonia, used to enhance savory flavor in foods such as soups, sauces and snacks.
A salt of magnesium and glutamic acid, an amino acid, used as a flavor enhancer that adds savory taste to foods.
A flavor enhancer made from guanylic acid salts, typically used with other savory ingredients to boost umami taste.
A flavor enhancer made from inosinic acid salts, often used alongside glutamates to intensify savory taste.
A flavor enhancer made from inosinic acid and potassium, used to intensify savory, meaty taste in foods.
A flavor enhancer made from the sodium salts of inosinic and guanylic acids, which are nucleotides. It is often derived from yeast or fish and can come from animal sources.
Maltol is a naturally occurring compound found in roasted malt and some fruits, used as a flavor enhancer to add a sweet, caramel-like taste.
Ethyl maltol is a synthetic compound similar to maltol, used as a flavor enhancer to give foods a sweet, fruity, or caramel-like taste.
A pair of related compounds: glycine, a simple amino acid, and its sodium salt, used as a sweetener, flavor enhancer and buffer in foods.
Glycine is the simplest amino acid, used in foods as a sweetener, flavor enhancer and buffering agent.
Leucine is an essential amino acid, used in food as a flavor enhancer and nutritional supplement.
A zinc salt of acetic acid, used as a firming agent and as a source of zinc in some foods.
A silicone mixture of dimethylpolysiloxane and methylphenylpolysiloxane polymers, used as an anti-foaming agent to reduce foam during food processing.
A silicone polymer made of repeating dimethylsiloxane units, used as an emulsifier to help oil and water mix in food.
A wax produced by honeybees, processed for use in food. It is used as a glazing agent, carrier, and stabilizer on confectionery and some other foods.
A wax obtained from the leaves of the candelilla shrub, used as a carrier, emulsifier and thickener, often as a glazing agent on confectionery.
A natural wax obtained from the leaves of the Brazilian carnauba palm, used as a carrier and coating agent in foods.
A resin secreted by the lac insect, processed into a glossy coating. It is used as a glazing agent on confectionery, fruit, and some other foods.
A man-made wax produced by chemical synthesis rather than from natural sources, used as a coating agent on foods such as confectionery and fruit to give a glossy finish.
A highly refined petroleum-derived oil that is colorless and odorless. It is used as a release agent, lubricant, and carrier in foods and coatings.
Petroleum jelly is a semi-solid mixture of hydrocarbons refined from crude oil, used in food as a glazing agent and release agent for coatings.
A hard, purified wax derived from petroleum, used as a glazing or coating agent that gives foods a protective, shiny surface.
A fine-grained, refined wax produced from petroleum, used as a glazing and coating agent on foods and their packaging surfaces.
A refined mineral wax derived from petroleum, used as a coating agent to give foods a protective, glossy finish.
A natural resin obtained from benzoin trees, used as a flavoring and as a coating agent in foods.
A natural wax obtained from the bran layer of rice, used as a coating and firming agent on foods.
A compound formed by combining a fatty acid with a fatty alcohol, used as a coating or glazing agent on foods such as fruit and confectionery.
A mixture of methyl esters of fatty acids, used as a food coating and release agent in packaged foods.
Lanolin is a waxy substance obtained from the wool of sheep, used as a glazing agent and coating for foods such as confectionery and fruit.
Calcium iodate is a calcium salt of iodic acid, used as a source of iodine in food.
Potassium iodate is an inorganic salt of potassium and iodine, used as a source of iodine and as a dough conditioner in some foods.
A reactive inorganic compound of nitrogen, oxygen and chlorine that is used as a food treatment agent in limited applications.
An amino acid, used as a flour treatment agent to modify dough texture and as a nutrient supplement in some foods.
A hydrochloride salt of the amino acid L-cysteine, used as a dough conditioner that softens gluten and improves dough handling in baked goods.
Potassium bromate is a white crystalline salt that was used as a flour treatment agent to strengthen dough and improve loaf volume in baked goods.
Chlorine is a chemical element in gaseous form used in food processing, for example as a sanitizing or bleaching agent.
A mixture of two nitrogen-containing compounds used as a dough conditioner and bleaching agent in baked goods and flour.
A synthetic organic compound used as a dough conditioner and blowing agent in some flour-based foods and baked goods.
Carbamide is another name for urea, a nitrogen-containing compound that is made synthetically and is used in food as a firming agent and dough conditioner.
Benzoyl peroxide is a chemical compound used in food as a preservative and as a bleaching agent for flour.
A white powder that is an inorganic peroxide of calcium, used as a flour treatment agent and to bleach or oxidize dough.
A colorless, odorless noble gas from the air, used as a propellant and packaging gas to displace oxygen and help preserve food.
A colorless, odorless noble gas used as a propellant and protective gas to package foods.
A colorless gas used as a propellant to dispense foods such as whipped toppings and sprays.
Nitrogen is an inert gas used as a propellant to push food out of aerosol cans, such as whipped toppings and sprays.
Nitrous oxide is a colorless gas used to pressurize aerosol cans, and in food it can also serve as a propellant gas for whipped products.
Butane is a flammable hydrocarbon gas that is used as a propellant to push food out of aerosol cans.
Isobutane is a flammable hydrocarbon gas used as a propellant in aerosol food containers and as a carrier for flavourings.
Propane is a hydrocarbon gas used as a propellant in aerosol food products, helping to push contents out of the container.
Oxygen is the gaseous element present in air, used in food packaging to fill containers as a propellant or to help preserve products.
A colorless, odorless gas used as a food additive for processing and packaging, where it acts as a propellant or carrier gas.
A calorie-free artificial sweetener made from acetoacetic acid and potassium, used to add sweetness to foods and drinks.
A synthetic dipeptide compound used as a high-intensity sweetener, roughly two hundred times sweeter than sugar, in diet beverages and foods.
A synthetic sugar substitute, present as the acid and its sodium or calcium salts, used to add sweetness with few or no calories.
A sugar alcohol made from sucrose, used as a bulk sweetener, stabilizer and thickener in sugar-free candies and baked goods.
Saccharin is a synthetic sweetener made from chemical compounds, used to add a sweet taste to foods and drinks with few calories.
Sucralose is a synthetic sweetener made by chemically modifying sugar, providing sweetness with no significant calories in the amounts used.
A sweet-tasting protein extracted from the katemfe fruit of West Africa, used as a sugar substitute in small amounts.
Glycyrrhizin is a sweet compound extracted from the root of the liquorice plant and is used as a sweetener in food.
A synthetic sweetener derived from citrus flavonoids, used to add intense sweetness in small amounts to foods and drinks.
A group of sweet compounds extracted from the leaves of the stevia plant, used as a high-intensity, low-calorie sweetener in foods and drinks.
Sweet compounds extracted from the leaves of the stevia plant, used as a zero-calorie sweetener.
Sweet compounds produced from the stevia plant through enzyme treatment, used as a high-intensity sweetener in foods and drinks.
Sweet stevia-derived compounds modified by adding glucose units, used as a high-intensity sweetener in foods and drinks.
Neotame is a synthetic sweetener, chemically related to aspartame, that provides a very intense sweet taste in small amounts.
A blend of the sweeteners aspartame and acesulfame potassium in salt form. It provides intense sweetness with very few calories.
A sugar-like sweetener that is a naturally occurring ketohexose, used to add sweetness with fewer calories than sucrose. Taxonomy lists it as derived from an animal source.
Polyglycitol syrup is a syrup made by hydrogenating a mixture of sugars and sugar alcohols, used as a sweetener with reduced sugar content.
A sugar alcohol made from maltose that acts as a sweetener, humectant, emulsifier and stabilizer, adding bulk and body to foods.
A sugar alcohol derived from maltose, used as a sweetener that also retains moisture, thickens and stabilizes foods.
A syrup containing a sugar alcohol made by hydrogenating starch, used as a bulking sweetener that helps retain moisture and texture.
A sugar alcohol produced by chemically reducing lactose, derived from milk. It provides sweetness, adds bulk, and helps thicken and emulsify food.
A sugar alcohol made by processing plant materials such as birch wood or corn cobs, used as a sweetener and to help keep foods moist and smooth.
Erythritol is a sugar alcohol with a sweet taste, used as a sweetener that also helps foods retain moisture.
Advantame is a synthetic intense sweetener, several hundred times sweeter than sucrose, used to add sweetness to foods and drinks in very small amounts.
An extract from the bark of the Quillaja saponaria tree, used as an emulsifier to keep oil and water mixed in beverages and other foods.
A group of mineral compounds, such as salts of sodium, potassium, calcium or phosphate, used in foods for many purposes including acidity control, leavening and texture.
Isomaltose is a sugar made of two glucose units linked together, produced by breaking down starch, and it is used to provide sweetness and bulk in foods.
An organic sulfur compound, also known as dimethyl sulfone, used as a dietary ingredient and in some food and beverage products.
Organic acids is a general term for a group of carbon-based acids, such as citric or lactic acid, that are used to adjust tartness and acidity in foods.
Potassium iodide is a salt of potassium and iodine, used as a source of iodine in food.
E364 is a designation for a group of compounds called fumaric acid esters or salts, not a single named substance, and it is used in food to regulate acidity or as a preservative.
E386 is disodium EDTA's calcium-free relative, a salt of edetic acid that binds metal ions to help preserve color, flavor, and freshness in foods.
